record.paper_title: The Future of Primordial Black Holes: Open Questions and Roadmap
record.original_question: Do PBHs cluster significantly after formation, and how does clustering alter binary merger rates, gravitational-wave signals observed by LIGO/Virgo and future detectors, microlensing and cosmic microwave background constraints, PBH spins, and the extrapolation from current simulations at redshift z ≈ 10^2 down to observationally relevant lower redshifts?

evidence.quote: How well can we ascertain the PBH clustering properties and therefore the GW signal from binary mergers via LIGO and future terrestrial GW interferometers?

Another open issue worth mentioning is the clustering of PBHs. It may significantly affect the merger rates of coalescing binaries and, consequently, the gravitational wave signal measured by the LIGO/Virgo collaboration and by future experiments.

If PBHs cluster or not is therefore an important question to address. A significant PBH clustering might also modify constraints arising from microlensing observations and from the cosmic microwave background. Clustering might also be relevant in determining PBH spins.

Current N-body simulations are limited to large redshifts z ∼ 102 and a chief challenge is how to extrapolate to lower redshifts relevant for some observational constraints. Analytical insight is certainly called for in understanding the complex evolution of the PBH population.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a cosmological population of primordial black holes (PBHs): compact objects hypothesized to form in the early Universe from the gravitational collapse of large density fluctuations, with a possibly extended mass function and a fractional abundance f_PBH = Ω_PBH/Ω_DM relative to the dark matter density. Let the spatial distribution of PBHs at formation be characterized by a two-point correlation function ξ(r), with the Poisson case corresponding to ξ ≡ 0; deviations from Poisson are referred to as "initial clustering." After formation, gravitational dynamics modifies the spatial distribution, leads to the formation of PBH halos/clusters, alters binary formation channels (early-Universe decoupling pairs, late-Universe dynamical capture, three-body hardening), and affects the population-level distribution of PBH spins.

Address the following:

(a) Quantify whether PBHs cluster significantly after formation, beyond the initial Poisson distribution, as a function of f_PBH, the PBH mass function, and any non-Gaussianity of the primordial perturbations sourcing them. Provide a predictive analytical or semi-analytical model for the evolution of the PBH correlation function ξ(r, z) from formation to redshift z ≈ 0.

(b) Determine how clustering modifies the merger rate R(z) of PBH binaries, including the relative contributions of early- and late-Universe channels, and produce a corresponding prediction for the stochastic and resolvable gravitational-wave signal observable by current (LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA) and future (Einstein Telescope, Cosmic Explorer, LISA) detectors.

(c) Determine how PBH clustering modifies the constraints on f_PBH derived from microlensing surveys and from cosmic microwave background spectral distortions and anisotropies.

(d) Determine how clustering, through repeated hierarchical mergers and dynamical interactions inside clusters, shapes the distribution of PBH spins.

(e) Develop a controlled method to extrapolate predictions from N-body simulations of PBH systems—currently feasible only down to redshifts of order z ∼ 10^2—to the much lower redshifts z ≲ 10 relevant for observational constraints, providing analytical insight into the long-term nonlinear evolution of the PBH population.
artifact.category_tag: primordial black hole clustering and merger rates
artifact.status_search_result: The question remains an active open research problem. Multiple recent works (2024–2026) study aspects of PBH clustering, redshift evolution of merger rates, and mass-ratio-modulated initial clustering, providing partial models (e.g., merger rate scaling ℛ ∝ (1+z)^β with β ≈ 1.4–2.2) and N-body simulations of PBH clusters, but a complete, predictive framework spanning clustering evolution, GW signatures, microlensing/CMB constraints, spin distribution, and extrapolation from z ∼ 10^2 to low redshift is not yet established.

status_evidence.title: Redshift evolution of primordial black hole merger rate
status_evidence.snippet: The PBH merger rate changes with redshift as ℛ ∝ (1 + z)^β, where β = 1.4 - 2.2, reflecting the influence of PBH clustering.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on quantifying the impact of clustering on the redshift evolution of the merger rate.

status_evidence.title: Primordial black holes with mass ratio-modulated initial clustering: merger suppression and projected constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Recent results account for variations in binary mass ratio and show that for broadly extended mass distributions, merger suppression is greatly reduced for binaries with high mass ratios.
status_evidence.claim: Active 2025–2026 research is still refining the effect of clustering on merger rates and constraints.

status_evidence.title: Primordial Black Hole clusters, phenomenology & implications
status_evidence.snippet: Review of PBH clusters, their formation, phenomenology, and implications for observations.
status_evidence.claim: Clustering phenomenology is recognized as an open, evolving topic with implications across observational channels.

status_evidence.title: The Clustering Dynamics of Primordial Black Holes in N-Body Simulations
status_evidence.snippet: N-body simulations of PBH clustering dynamics.
status_evidence.claim: N-body approaches remain limited and motivate continued work on extrapolation to low redshift.
